title: Tekkonkinkreet: Black & White
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Two orphans, the tough, ruthless Black and the childlike, dreamy White, rule the streets of Treasure Town, a decaying city run by gangs. When Snake, a corporate figure, moves to demolish the town for a theme park and sends enhanced killers after them, White is wounded and taken into custody, and Black, alone, slides into madness through a violent alter ego before the two are reunited (Wikipedia).
life_message: People need each other to stay whole: innocence and toughness each fall apart without the other.

content.note: Street fights, assassination attempts, White kills an attacker in self-defense, Kimura murders his mentor and is killed (Wikipedia; AniList Gangs/Yakuza, MU Mature).
Enhanced killers hunt two children; Black's hallucinations (Wikipedia).
Kimura's pregnant wife; Nudity tag rank 26 (AniList) (to verify).

Black descends into madness and a destructive alter ego, the Minotaur (Wikipedia; AniList Denpa/Philosophy tags).
Orphan children mug, steal and fight to survive (Viz blurb via AniList, Wikipedia).

dominant: Innocence and corruption; friendship as salvation; a city lost to violence and redevelopment

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Black treats the town as his turf and answers yakuza enforcers by assault (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Street orphans outside any rule; police neurotic and ineffective (Viz blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Everything turns on the two boys' bond; the city is hostile.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Yakuza hierarchy shown destructive; Kimura's loyalty to his mentor ends in murder.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Old Treasure Town valued over the planned theme park.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Mugging and fighting to survive (Viz blurb).

folkways.japan: Yakuza loyalty codes and the oyabun-mentor bond broken by Kimura reflect Japanese crime-fiction norms, described here rather than endorsed by the story.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia cites Scott Campbell praising its thematic ambiguity and Deb Aoki on its poignant exploration of innocence and corruption.
delivery.note: The pair act as two halves of a theme rather than mouthpieces, and the story leaves much for the reader to interpret.

winners_losers: Black and White survive and end reunited on a beach; Snake is killed by Kimura, who is then assassinated. The bond between the boys gets the sympathy, while gang violence and Snake's plan bring ruin (Wikipedia).
